title: 3.3.24 Arrays
description: Work with lists of values: create, add, remove, and iterate.

steps.title: Create an array
steps.instructions: Declare an array called fruits with at least three items, written in square brackets.

steps.title: Add and remove elements
steps.instructions: Add one more item to the end of the array with push, then remove one item with pop.

steps.title: Iterate with a loop
steps.instructions: Use a for loop to visit every item in the array and log each one.

steps.title: Search with a loop
steps.instructions: Write a loop that compares each item to the one you want with ===, and log whether it was found.

steps.title: Write a counting function
steps.instructions: Write a function called countFruit(fruits, name) that loops over the array it is given and returns how many items are exactly name (compare with ===). Return the count instead of printing it, then log countFruit(fruits, "apple") to try it.

steps.title: Write a filtering function
steps.instructions: Write a function called longFruits(fruits, minLength) that builds and returns a NEW array holding only the items whose length is minLength or more, in their original order. Leave the array you were given untouched, then log the result.

requirements.title: Create array
requirements.description: Declare an array using square brackets. Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: An array is a list in square brackets, such as let items = [1, 2, 3];. See Reading 3.3.2.

requirements.title: Use push
requirements.description: Add elements using .push(). Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: .push() adds an item to the end of an array. Call it on your array with the value in parentheses.

requirements.title: Use pop
requirements.description: Remove an element using .pop(). Help: 3.3.2 (Array Basics: Index, push, pop)
requirements.hint: .pop() removes the last item. Call it on your array with empty parentheses.

requirements.title: Iterate with a for loop
requirements.description: Loop through the array with a for loop that has something in its body. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays)
requirements.hint: A for loop visits each position in turn. Put at least one statement inside its braces. See Reading 3.3.5.

requirements.title: Search with a comparison
requirements.description: Inside a loop, compare each item to the one you want with === (or use includes / indexOf) and act on it. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays)
requirements.hint: Inside the loop, use if with === to compare each item to the one you want. See Reading 3.3.5.

requirements.title: countFruit returns how many times a name appears
requirements.description: countFruit(fruits, name) returns the number of items in the array that are exactly name, and 0 when there are none. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: countFruit must return a number: add 1 to a count each time an item === name, and return the count after the loop.

requirements.title: longFruits returns a new array of the long names
requirements.description: longFruits(fruits, minLength) returns a new array with only the items whose length is minLength or more, in order, and does not change the array it was given. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: Build a separate result array, push an item only when its length is at least minLength, and return the result. Do not push onto or remove from the array you were given.

cases.description: a name exactly minLength long counts
